title: 第二十五章 开门第二十四章 开幕
lines: 第二十五章开门
第二天，沈南枝到展馆的时候，门口已经有人在等了。
不是别人，是昨天那个刘建国。他换了一身深灰色的西装，头发打了摩丝，手里拿着一个公文包，站在台阶上看手表。看见沈南枝过来，他迎上来两步。
“沈老板，我带我老婆来了。”
他身后站着一个女人，四十岁左右，烫着小卷发，穿着一件暗红色的呢子大衣，脖子上围着一条浅灰色的围巾。长得不算好看，但气质不错，站在那儿腰板很直。
沈南枝把展台的灯打开。刘建国的老婆走到展柜前面，弯下腰看银花。她看得很仔细，每一件都拿起来对着光看，翻过来看背面，又用手指摸了摸花瓣的边缘。
“这个戴久了会不会变黑？”她问。
“银饰都会氧化，戴久了发黑是正常的。用牙膏擦一擦就亮了。”沈南枝从柜台下面拿出一块银布，“用这个擦也行，买的时候送一块。”
女人拿起那串粗犷款的野藤项链，挂在脖子上试了试。站在镜子前面左看右看，又摘下来。
“这个太粗了，我戴不合适。”她转向银花系列，拿起那款项链，“这个呢？”
沈南枝帮她戴上。银花垂在锁骨的位置，花瓣在灯光下亮闪闪的。女人对着镜子看了好一会儿，又转了个身。
“多少钱？”
“项链二百八，耳环一百六，一套四百四。”
女人看了看刘建国。刘建国点了下头。女人把项链摘下来，放在柜台上。
“要了。耳环也要。”
沈南枝把东西装进包装盒里，刘建国从包里掏出钱，一张一张数出来。四百四，不多不少。沈南枝找了零，把袋子递过去。
“谢谢刘总。”
刘建国接过袋子，笑了笑，走了。
何婉清在旁边把第一笔订单记在本子上，抬头看了沈南枝一眼，嘴角动了一下。
开门了。
九点多的时候，展馆里的人多起来了。沈南枝的展台前面开始排队——不是排长队，但一直有人。大部分是来看的，问价的，试戴的。买的不多，但每一个停下来的人都看得很认真。
有个二十出头的姑娘看中了一对银花耳环，拿在手里翻来覆去看了五分钟，最后咬着牙掏了一百六。她说她是省城百货大楼的售货员，一个月工资才一百八，这一对耳环花了她将近一个月的工资。但她戴上就不肯摘了，对着镜子照了又照，走的时候还在回头看。
有个五十多岁的老太太，穿着一件洗得发白的蓝布褂子，在展台前面站了很久，一直盯着那件最贵的胸针看。胸针是银丝编的藤蔓，上面镶了三颗紫水晶，标价五百八。沈南枝看她站了那么久，问了一句“阿姨，您要不要试试？”
老太太摇了摇头，走了。过了半个小时又回来了，还是站在那儿看。沈南枝把胸针拿出来递给她，她接过去摸了摸，放在手心里看了好一会儿，还回来，又走了。第三次回来的时候，她从口袋里掏出一个用手帕包着的钱包，一层一层打开，里面的钱有十块的、五块的、一块的，还有几张毛票。她数了半天，抬头看着沈南枝。
“姑娘，能便宜点不？四百五行不行？”
沈南枝看了她一眼。老太太的手枯瘦，指关节粗大，指甲缝里有泥。
“您买给谁的？”
“我闺女。她下个月结婚，我想给她买个像样的东西。她从小就喜欢这些亮晶晶的。”
沈南枝沉默了两秒。
“四百五，给您包起来。”
老太太的手抖了一下，把手帕里的钱又数了一遍，递过来。沈南枝接过钱，把胸针装进盒子里，用绒布包好，又拿了一张红色的包装纸在外面裹了一层。
老太太接过盒子，抱在怀里，走了。
何婉清在旁边看着，没说话。等老太太走远了，她才开口。
“那件胸针的成本就不止四百五。”
“我知道。”
“那你还卖？”
沈南枝把钱收进抽屉里。
“她闺女结婚。”
何婉清看了她一眼，没再说什么。

Chapter 25 Open the door
The next day, when Shen Nanzhi arrived at the exhibition hall, there were already people waiting at the door.
It was none other than the Liu Jianguo from yesterday. He changed into a dark gray suit, wore mousse on his hair, held a briefcase in his hand, and stood on the steps looking at his watch. Seeing Shen Nanzhi coming, he took two steps forward to greet her.
"Boss Shen, I brought my wife here."
Behind him stood a woman, about forty years old, with curly hair, wearing a dark red woolen coat and a light gray scarf around her neck. He's not good-looking, but he has a good temperament and stands straight.
Shen Nanzhi turned on the lights in the booth. Liu Jianguo's wife walked to the display cabinet and bent down to look at the silver flowers. She looked at each piece carefully, holding it up to the light, turning it over to look at the back, and touching the edges of the petals with her fingers.
"Will it turn black if worn for a long time?" she asked.
"Silver jewelry will oxidize. It is normal for it to turn black after being worn for a long time. Just wipe it with toothpaste and it will shine." Shen Nanzhi took out a piece of silver cloth from under the counter. "You can also use this to wipe it. You will get one when you buy it."
The woman picked up the rough wild rattan necklace and hung it around her neck to try it on. Stand in front of the mirror, look left and right, and then take it off.
"This one is too thick and doesn't fit me." She turned to the silver flower series and picked up the necklace, "What about this one?"
Shen Nanzhi helped her put it on. Silver flowers hang down on the collarbone, and the petals sparkle under the light. The woman looked at the mirror for a long time and then turned around.
"How much?"
"Two hundred and eight for the necklace, one hundred and six for the earrings, and four hundred and four for the set."
The woman looked at Liu Jianguo. Liu Jianguo nodded. The woman took off the necklace and placed it on the counter.
"I want it. I want the earrings too."
Shen Nanzhi put the things into the packaging box, and Liu Jianguo took out the money from his bag and counted them one by one. Four hundred and four, no more, no less. Shen Nanzhi found change and handed the bag over.
"Thank you, Mr. Liu."
Liu Jianguo took the bag, smiled, and left.
He Wanqing wrote down the first order in a notebook nearby, looked up at Shen Nanzhi, and moved the corner of her mouth.
The door is open.
At around nine o'clock, there were more people in the exhibition hall. A queue began to form in front of Shen Nanzhi’s booth—not a long queue, but there were always people. Most of them come to see, ask about prices, and try on items. Not much was bought, but everyone who stopped looked at it seriously.
There was a girl in her early twenties who took a fancy to a pair of silver flower earrings. She looked at them over and over for five minutes, and finally gritted her teeth and took out a hundred and sixty dollars. She said that she was a saleswoman in a department store in the provincial capital and her monthly salary was only 180 yuan. This pair of earrings cost her nearly a month's salary. But she refused to take it off after putting it on. She looked in the mirror again and again, and she was still looking back when she left.
There was an old lady in her fifties, wearing a washed blue cloth gown, who stood in front of the booth for a long time, staring at the most expensive brooch. The brooch is a vine made of silver wire, with three amethysts inlaid on it. The price is five hundred and eighty. Shen Nanzhi saw her standing there for so long and asked, "Auntie, do you want to try it?"
The old lady shook her head and left. I came back half an hour later and still stood there watching. Shen Nanzhi took out the brooch and handed it to her. She took it and touched it, looked at it for a while, returned it, and left again. When she came back for the third time, she took out a wallet wrapped in a handkerchief from her pocket and opened it layer by layer. There were ten yuan, five yuan, one yuan, and a few dimes in it. She counted for a long time and looked up at Shen Nanzhi.
"Girl, can it be cheaper? Four hundred and five cents?"
Shen Nanzhi glanced at her. The old lady's hands were skinny, her knuckles were thick, and there was mud between her nails.
"Who did you buy it for?"
"My daughter. She is getting married next month, and I want to buy her something decent. She has liked these shiny things since she was a child."
Shen Nanzhi was silent for two seconds.
"Four hundred and five, wrap it up for you."
The old lady's hand shook, she counted the money in the handkerchief again, and handed it over. Shen Nanzhi took the money, put the brooch into the box, wrapped it in flannel, and wrapped it with a piece of red wrapping paper.
The old lady took the box, held it in her arms, and left.
He Wanqing looked on without saying a word. She didn't speak until the old lady walked away.
"That brooch cost more than four hundred and five hundred."
"I know."
"Then you still sell it?"
Shen Nanzhi put the money into the drawer.
"Her daughter is getting married."
He Wanqing glanced at her and said nothing more.
